title: Anonymous: Million Masks

description.main: A photographic record of the Million Mask March, the annual November 5th street action held in the name of the hacktivist collective Anonymous, by the photographer Anthony Tafuro. Tafuro followed the march from 2013 to 2017; powerHouse Books, 2018, 160 pages.
description.extended:
A photographic record of the Million Mask March, the annual November 5th street action held in the name of the hacktivist collective Anonymous, by the photographer Anthony Tafuro.

Tafuro followed the march from 2013 to 2017, the years in which thousands gathered in cities around the world for it. He photographed masked participants in the street and in the meetings and gatherings held around the demonstrations, and the pictures run alongside a short history of Guy Fawkes and of the stylised mask that became the group's public face. The cover carries the Anonymous emblem, a headless suit before a globe and laurel wreath, on a green ground. 160 pages, hardcover, published by powerHouse Books, Brooklyn, in 2018.

Tafuro photographs subcultures that keep their faces hidden. His earlier book for the same publisher, BA. KU.: Kult Skating / Dark Rituals (2015), documented the Barrier Kult, a masked skateboarding crew. Anonymous: Million Masks carries that interest in concealed identity into political protest. It sits in the Surveillance Index as a document of the mask as disguise and as shared signal in public space.
description.artist_bio: Anthony Tafuro is a New York photographer who documents subcultures that keep their faces hidden. His first book, BA. KU. (powerHouse Books, 2015, ISBN 9781576877388), documented the Barrier Kult, a masked skateboarding crew. Anonymous: Million Masks (2018) is his second title with the publisher.
